name: Should I replace or improve the bathroom fan when replacing my shower?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace or improve the bathroom fan when replacing my shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan ventilation as part of the replacement when the bathroom stays damp, mirrors remain fogged, mildew repeatedly returns, or the existing fan is ineffective. Context: A new shower cannot compensate for poor moisture removal, and changes to electrical or ducting may add scope. Key factors: fan performance; duct routing; controls; makeup air; window use; ceiling height; and whether the fan vents outdoors. Practical guidance: Describe the room’s moisture symptoms during the consultation and ask whether the existing ventilation should be evaluated before finishes close. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate bathroom construction details with related electrical or layout work when included in the approved scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider improving ventilation if the room stays damp, the mirror remains fogged, or mildew returns despite cleaning. A new shower will not fix inadequate moisture removal. Ask whether the fan, duct route, controls, and outdoor venting should be evaluated before walls or ceilings are finished.
